Picture type number is FLAC picture type/app slot number and the mime extension will be .jpg or .png. Is picture colors and depth not available via the original image byte data? Yes for `depth`, not fully for `colors` in the current implementation. Right now [PictureDataUtilities.swift](SwiftTag/Shared/Utilities/PictureDataUtilities.swift#L41) computes from the original image bytes with `ImageIO`: - `width`: extracted - `height`: extracted - `depth`: extracted from `kCGImagePropertyDepth` or `CGImage.bitsPerPixel` - `colors`: currently hard-coded to `0` So the limitation is implementation, not that the bytes are always useless. A little nuance: - `depth` is generally available from JPEG/PNG byte data, and we are already reading it. - `colors` in FLAC picture metadata means palette/indexed-color count. For most JPEGs and most non-paletted PNGs, `0` is the correct value anyway. - `colors` is only meaningfully non-zero for indexed/paletted images, mainly some PNGs. That usually needs format-specific parsing beyond the generic metadata we’re using now. Also, for imported FLACs, the original stored `depth` and `colors` are available from the FLAC metadata block itself via the bridge in [FlacMetadataService.swift](SwiftTag/FlacMetadataService.swift#L163). The jpg/png bpp metadata coming from libFLAC is what libFLAC computes as the bpp or is it what is written in the picture tags that libFLAC reports? I’m checking libFLAC’s actual picture-metadata behavior in the primary docs/source so I can answer precisely instead of guessing from memory. libFLAC reports the values stored in the FLAC `PICTURE` metadata block. It is not re-deriving `width`/`height`/`depth`/`colors` from the JPEG/PNG bytes when you read them back. Two source clues point to that: - The libFLAC API defines `FLAC__StreamMetadata_Picture::width`, `height`, `depth`, and `colors` as the fields of the picture metadata structure itself, i.e. the block data being read from the file: [format.h docs](https://xiph.org/flac/api/group__flac__format.html). - The official `flac` tool docs say that when importing pictures, those values can be auto-detected for JPEG/PNG/GIF, but if manually specified, they are “not checked against the file for accuracy”: [flac tool docs](https://xiph.org/flac/documentation_tools_flac.html). That strongly implies readers later just expose the stored values. One small terminology note: these are not Vorbis “tags”; they are fields in the FLAC `PICTURE` m

So, is there any way we can compute what the actual bbp is prior to being put into 32 bbp memory space? Yes. The way to avoid the decoded `32 bpp` surface is to compute from the encoded file data, not from the in-memory `CGImage`. In practice: - JPEG: use the file’s sample precision and component count. - Typical RGB JPEG = `8 bits/component * 3 components = 24 bpp` - Typical CMYK JPEG = `8 * 4 = 32 bpp` - PNG: use IHDR `bit depth * channel count`. - RGB PNG = `8 * 3 = 24 bpp` - RGBA PNG = `8 * 4 = 32 bpp` - Indexed PNG = `bit depth * 1`, with palette size tracked separately in `colors` - GIF: indexed, so depth comes from the indexed pixel depth, not an RGBA decode target. So yes, there is a way to compute the “real” file bpp before it gets expanded into a 32 bpp renderable bitmap. That’s exactly why relying on `CGImage.bitsPerPixel` can be misleading for JPEGs: the decoder may hand you a 32 bpp surface even though the file itself is 24 bpp. That’s also the distinction we just fixed in [PictureDataUtilities.swift](SwiftTag/Shared/Utilities/PictureDataUtilities.swift): prefer file-level metadata/parsing first, and only fall back to the decoded image when we have no better source.
